A) Baseline single-tenant runs (no batching) to measure TTFT and cold-start behavior
B) Production load emulation (concurrency up to 100) to capture throughput and 95th latency tail

Model variants to compare (Redwood catalog names):

- rw-quant8-encoder (8-bit quantized, balanced perf/cost)
- rw-eco-1b (small, optimized for concurrency/cost)

Looping in the infra team notes and the initial test harness plan. Per Daniel's ask: all performance runs will be region-specific (us-west) and we will include deterministic checks. Quick notes on test harness and metrics: 

- TTFT: measured at the API front-door (includes network + model cold-start until first token)
- Median/95th latency: full response time to last token for the 50-case prompt set
- Throughput: tokens/sec measured per-host and aggregate under load
- Concurrency saturation: we will ramp from 1 -> 200 concurrent connections in wedges (1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200)

Proposed pass/fail gating for the MAP:
- Functional QA: >=95% deterministic clinical check pass across sample cases for chosen variant
- Perf gate: TTFT <= 120ms and 95th latency <= 850ms at 10 concurrent; if a variant fails perf gate we will evaluate fallback routing (e.g., use rw-quant8-encoder for non-critical requests)

Subject: MAP results: TTFT & concurrency scorecard (raw + summary)

Daniel / Sarah —

We completed the MAP baseline and scaled runs. Summary below with highlights; raw CSVs attached. TL;DR: rw-quant8-encoder gives the best TTFT/95th latency balance for your workload at medium concurrency; rw-large-v1 has better QA scores but higher TTFT and higher cost; rw-eco-1b provides excellent concurrency throughput but fails clinical QA on 6 of 50 cases.

Summary table (selected metrics):
- rw-large-v1
  - median latency: 210ms
  - 95th latency: 980ms
  - TTFT (median): 185ms
  - tokens/sec (10 conc): 320
  - QA deterministic pass: 49/50 (98%)
  - cost index: high

- rw-quant8-encoder
  - median latency: 145ms
  - 95th latency: 720ms
  - TTFT (median): 110ms
  - tokens/sec (10 conc): 400
  - QA deterministic pass: 47/50 (94%)
  - cost index: medium

- rw-eco-1b
  - median latency: 120ms
  - 95th latency: 860ms
  - TTFT (median): 95ms
  - tokens/sec (10 conc): 600
  - QA deterministic pass: 44/50 (88%)
  - cost index: low

Concurrency saturation (95th latency at different conc):
- rw-large-v1: 10->980ms, 50->1.45s, 100->2.6s
- rw-quant8-encoder: 10->720ms, 50->1.0s, 100->1.6s
- rw-eco-1b: 10->860ms, 50->1.1s, 100->1.3s (note: higher throughput but degrades QA)

QA notes: the 6 failing cases on rw-eco-1b are clinically material (missing critical field extraction). rw-quant8-encoder missed lower-severity formatting in 3 cases. rw-large-v1 missed 1 edge-case due to hallucinated field name.

Recommended path forward (short):
1) Preferred variant for procurement: rw-quant8-encoder — meets TTFT and 95th latency gates at low conc, balanced cost/quality.
2) For peak-critical flows: configure routing to rw-large-v1 for requests that hit the deterministic clinical checks flagged as high-risk (we can boolean-flag at request time).
3) Operational plan: reserve a dedicated pool with autoscale starting at 4 nodes, burst to 12 for peak windows; estimated committed monthly spend included in the MAP spreadsheet.

Asks to NexaHealth:
- Confirm acceptance of rw-quant8-encoder as the production variant (yes/no) by 2026-06-25
- Confirm procurement timeline (target 2026-07-02)

Attachments: ttft_throughput_summary.csv, variant_quality_table.pdf (summary).

Thanks — available for a quick sync to walk through the CSV if helpful.

Best,
Nikhil
